comparison: Matched progression: Rung 1 pure SGD (2/13, 2 NaN) -> Rung 2 SGD+secant (4/13) -> Rung 3a SGD-on-G (5/13) -> Rung 3b SGD-on-G+secant (9/15) vs unified-v11 (16/16).
conclusion: Rung 3b (law4_sgd_g_secant_equil_d: pure unnormalized SGD + Law 4 G secant trust band on G, exact unified_v11_equil on D & row-normalized prior, 0 G per-layer norm, 0 G MP, 0 G NS, 0 G states) scores 9/15 executed PASS (6 numerical FAIL, 0 NaN/TIMEOUT, 1 prereq-gated grid100_mlp16) on r4-occam-ablation-v1. Adding ONLY the generator secant band to Rung 3a (5/13) flips 4 tasks to PASS: nash_overpowered_generator_ring16 (8/16 hq=0.3672 -> 16/16 hq=0.9751), ring16_acquisition (14/16 -> 16/16 hq=0.9814), gaussian1d_smoke (ks=0.0475), and zero_tanh_smoke (mae=0.0020), joining img_bars4 (4/4 hq=1.0), nash_overpowered_critic (16/16 hq=0.9648), t3_iso_horizon_saddle_shift (4/4 hq=0.9609), and vector_unequal_mass/width (0.9951/0.9998). Directly answers 'Or SGD on G if impedance mismatch isnt a problem?': YES for shallow/balanced, Conv2d 4-mode images, saddle-shift, and >500x imbalanced Nash, but NO for multi-scale/multi-module/stiff generator regimes — pure SGD on G still fails 6 tasks (grid100 prec=0.4655/ctr=1.7461 gating mlp16, five_word_joint_smoke 3/5 modes, model_ddgan_gaussian_chain t1_q0=1.4281, zero_tanh_rail_escape mae=0.0031, gaussian1d_stability ks=0.0452, t3_iso_scale_mass_8x eig=0.4035).

hypothesis: Evaluate law4-sgd-g-secant-equil-d (Rung 3b (Asymmetric Hybrid — Pure SGD + Law 4 G Secant Band on G, Equilibrated D & Prior): apply pure unnormalized SGD wrapped by Law 4 generator secant trust band (delta_g_min/max) on G while keeping exact unified_v11_equil on D and row-normalized prior.) across all 16 surgical probes of r4-occam-ablation-v1 under protocol seed 0 (lr=0.014, d_lr_mult=1.5, prior_lr_mult=2.9 held identical to unified-v11) to establish the exact causal SGD & G/D asymmetry ladder.
next_action: Conclude Rung 4 (causal reverse control law4-equil-g-sgd-d) and Rung 5 (zero-state layerwise Frobenius-MP SGD law4-frob-sgd-mp).
